newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs steady-$1.50 lower - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs steady-$1.50 lower - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Wednesday were steady to mostly $0.50 to $1.50 lower, dealers said.
Prices were pressured by steep declines Tuesday in pork product values more than adequate hog supplies, they said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota, hogs sold $1.00 lower at $58.00 to $58.50 per cwt in the country and $59.50 to $60.50 for hogs delivered to the plant, according to the dealers.
Illinois hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower, but could slip further as the day progresses, with $59.00 to $60.00 paid in the country and $60.50 to $61.00 at plants.

Indiana hogs sold $1.50 lower in light activity, with a top of $57.00 in the country and $59.50 at plants. Prices were weakened by hefty marketings on Tuesday, which provided packers with enough hogs to get this morning's operations going, a dealer said.
Ohio hogs were steady at $57.50 to $58.50 in the country and $59.00 to $60.00 at plants.
Outlooks for continued soft pork product prices lent further weakness, they said.
Pork cut-out values on Tuesday were quoted down $1.11 to $1.15 per cwt, USDA reported.
